title: AutoMat: Physics-Guided Agentic Reasoning for Solving Ill-Posed Inverse Microscopy Problems
claim: An LLM agent orchestrates a pool of specialized tools to turn raw inputs into optimized outputs, and beats baselines on error metrics.
layout: 2 columns: vertical top-to-bottom flow left, line and radar plots right
description: The left column is a vertical pipeline. A purple input box, 'Raw STEM image (with text input)', splits into a gray text-prompt box and a grayscale microscopy image. A big arrow leads to a green 'LLM Agent' box with a robot icon. Two curved arrows from the agent point into a blue rounded 'Tools Pool' containing four dashed boxes: image denoising, candidate structure selection, atomic structure reconstruction (STEM2CIF), and property prediction and structure optimization. A second arrow leads to a yellow output box with a 3D crystal lattice render, a CIF label and a formation energy value. The right column has two plots. The top is a multi-series line chart of tiered MAE for several models, with AutoMat highlighted near the low end. The bottom is a radar chart over tiered RMSD, correlation coefficient (C.C) and structure similarity (S.S) metrics.
caption: Overview of AutoMat. The left part shows a failure-aware reasoning controller that composes four modules—pattern-adaptive denoising, template selection (state-triggered auxiliary branch), atomic reconstruction (STEM2CIF), and MLIP-based relaxation/property prediction—into a closed-loop verification workflow. The right panel presents a line chart and radar plot comparing different models in terms of energy and structural errors.
abstract: Reconstructing atomistic crystal structures from a single noisy STEM projection is an ill-posed inverse problem: multiple lattices can explain similar contrast, and purely feed-forward models cannot verify physical validity. We present AutoMat , a failure-aware agentic controller that performs inference-time hypothesis search with closed-loop verification to convert Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (STEM) images into simulation-ready crystal structures and downstream properties. AutoMat composes perception and physics modules—pattern-adaptive denoising, physics-guided template retrieval as a state-dependent auxiliary branch , symmetry-constrained atomic reconstruction, and MLIP-based relaxation/validation—and triggers rollback-and-retry when verification fails. For systematic evaluation, we introduce STEM2Mat-Bench , a benchmark dataset containing 450+ annotated samples. Performance is assessed using lattice root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), formation energy mean absolute error (MAE), and structure matching accuracy. Results demonstrate that AutoMat outperforms existing approaches including SOTA models, specialized domain tools, and closed-source multimodal large models. This work establishes a direct pathway from microscopic characterization to atomic-scale modeling, addressing a fundamental challenge in materials science.
